why: T48: the candidate-distance clamp ran before the cutoff test, so two collapsed atoms became a pair at exactly 1.0 A and entered the is_short cell the head learned to read as a bond. This records what the new predicate rejects on real geometry, on the synthetic collapse, and at the two distances cfm_generated_geometry_defect.json measured.

train_cfm_yuelbond_wasserstein.py: --bond-clash-reject (default ON) / --bond-clash-ratio (default 0.7); threaded into CFMJointModel and all four head classes
feature schema gains bond_clash_reject / bond_clash_ratio; the per-epoch generation block gains the same two keys
YuelBondDecodeResult gains clash_rejected_pairs, populated on both the normal and the empty-edge return

radius_table.note: deliberately generous: an unknown element is rejected less often, which fails toward keeping a candidate

not_measured.the_143_generated_pairs: cfm_generated_geometry_defect.json counted 143 hard-clash pairs on 24 generated clouds that were never written to disk, so they cannot be replayed. The predicate is pinned at the artifact's two measured means instead, and the population check stays UNMEASURED.
not_measured.effect_on_a_shipped_pool: needs a re-decode against a checkpoint (T29). Not inferred from the synthetic case.
